# NeoSatoshi Card Recognition API

> Card recognition API for Pokémon, One Piece, Disney Lorcana, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Magic: The Gathering, Star Wars: Unlimited, Digimon Card Game, Cyberpunk TCG, Riftbound, football (soccer) and basketball (NBA, EuroLeague) cards: send a photo, get JSON with set, number, rarity, Cardmarket ID and daily prices. Made by NeoSatoshi (NeoGen Solutions GmbH, Bern, Switzerland).

## Call

* Endpoint: POST https://europe-west1-neosatoshi.cloudfunctions.net/detectApi
* Header: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
* Public demo key (intentionally public, no signup, 10 detections per day per network): nsk_live_9c253fbed995042a98280ad13e5c47d3c4a59c9b4f0f7274
* Body (JSON): {"image": "<base64 JPEG or PNG, max 12 MB>", "tcg": "pokemon"}
* Alternative body: {"image_url": "https://...", "tcg": "pokemon"} (public https URL to a JPEG or PNG, max 12 MB)
* tcg values: pokemon (default), onepiece, lorcana, yugioh, magic, star_wars_unlimited, digimon, cyberpunk, riftbound, football, basketball
* Default: one JSON body. One card usually takes about 4 seconds, about 10 to 12 seconds on the first request after a quiet period; a binder page with 9 cards about 17 seconds. Client timeout: at least 120 seconds.
* Optional streaming: add "stream": true (or the header Accept: text/event-stream) to get Server-Sent Events: accepted, progress, card (each card as soon as it is recognised), then done (the same body as the JSON response) or error. Same cost. A reconnect is a new, charged detection.

## Games and card languages

* Pokémon (pokemon): English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese. Several cards per photo, binder pages work, best up to about 20.
* One Piece (onepiece): English, Japanese. Several cards per photo, binder pages work.
* Disney Lorcana (lorcana): English, German, French, Italian. Several cards per photo, binder pages work.
* Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG (yugioh): English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese. Not OCG. Several cards per photo, binder pages work.
* Magic: The Gathering (magic): English, German, French, Italian, Spanish. Several cards per photo, binder pages work.
* Star Wars: Unlimited (star_wars_unlimited): English, German, French, Italian, Spanish. Several cards per photo, binder pages work.
* Digimon Card Game (digimon): English, Japanese. Several cards per photo, binder pages work. Recognised by card number and name; alternative arts share the number, the printing comes from the picture or is picked from the alternatives. Older Digimon products (the 1999 card game, the 2000 trading cards) are not recognised.
* Cyberpunk TCG by WeirdCo (cyberpunk): English, French. Several cards per photo, binder pages work. Beta (Kickstarter) and Retail base cards share the same art, only the β before the number tells them apart (beta flag); when the photo cannot tell, the printing is picked from the alternatives.
* Riftbound, the League of Legends TCG by Riot Games (riftbound): English; French and Chinese prints are recognized without a price (review reason language_not_listed). Several cards per photo, binder pages work; PSA, BGS and CGC slab labels are read (TAG, ACE and PCG are not). Detection only: the card search, the lookup and corrections do not cover Riftbound (400 unsupported_tcg).
* One game per photo: send the matching tcg.
* Football (soccer) cards (football): Topps, Panini and other makers. Several card fronts per photo (binder pages work, best up to about 20), JPEG or PNG up to 4 MB, about 6 to 25 seconds. No card language.
* Basketball cards (basketball): NBA from Panini and Topps (mainly seasons 2018-19 to 2026-27 plus some older releases) and Panini EuroLeague sets from 2023-24; not WNBA, college, G League or NBL. Works like football: same fields, limits and credits, card_id bk-..., several card fronts per photo, up to 4 MB, no prices yet.

## Response

{request_id, count, cards[], credits{remaining}, correction{request_id, until, search_endpoint, endpoint}} for your own key; the public demo key gets demo{limit_per_day, remaining_today} instead of credits.

Each card: name, language, tcg (absent for Pokémon), card_id, card_index, set{id, ptcgo_code or code, name, number}, rarity, cardmarket_id, prices{cardmarket{trend, low, avg7, avg30, currency EUR}, tcgplayer (USD, where available)}, images{small, large}, confidence (0 to 1, a fixed step per match method, not a probability), image_quality{blurred, unusual_dimensions}, alternatives[] (score is a similarity inside this search, another scale than confidence: never pick by score alone), review{needed, reasons[], search}.

Game-specific: Pokémon name_ja, name_ko, name_zh, reverse_holo, first_edition, special_variant, possible_variants[] {key, label, special_variant, cardmarket_id (integer), price{avg30, avg7, low, trend, idProduct, updatedAt; lowPrice and trendPrice deprecated}}, price_basis (normal, reverse_holo, first_edition, special_variant: what prices.cardmarket describes), prices.cardmarket (the version the card is) plus cardmarket_normal (plain card), cardmarket_reverse (reverse holo family) and tcgplayer{market, currency USD}; cardmarket_id is the product of that version. One Piece card_id (for example OP01-003). Lorcana version, full_name, name_en, prices.cardmarket_foil. Yu-Gi-Oh! passcode, set.code, edition, price_versions, *_unconfirmed flags. Magic printing, prices.cardmarket_foil, TCGplayer foil price. Digimon card_key (the card number, for example BT1-025), print_id (the printing, for example BT1-025_P1), name_en, type, level, colors, set.code, variant, parallel_index, finishes, print_unconfirmed, number_unconfirmed; card_id is dg-<print_id> (English), dg-ja-<print_id> (Japanese) or dg-c-<number> while the printing is open (no price then, the printings come as alternatives, each priced); Cardmarket prices for English and Japanese printings, TCGplayer for English only. Cyberpunk card_key (the card, for example v-streetkid), print_id (set code + printed number without the β, for example WNC-132; the Beta WNCB-132 has the same art), subtitle, name_en, type, color, cost, set.code, set.number (as printed: 132, B132 on a Beta, 004a), finish (normal or foil, fixed per printing: Rare and above are foil), finishes, is_foil, beta, print_unconfirmed, number_unconfirmed; card_id is cp-<print_id> (English), cp-fr-<print_id> (French) or cp-c-<card_key> while the printing is open (no price then, the printings come as alternatives, each priced); Cardmarket prices for English and French cards (French takes the price of the same Cardmarket product), TCGplayer for English only. Riftbound card_key (the card, for example kaisa-daughter-of-the-void, one card in every printing), print_id (set code + printed number: OGN-066, OGN-066a alternate art, OGN-299* signed, VEN-R02 rune, UNL-T02-T05 a double-sided token), subtitle, name_en, type, domain[], cost, set.code, set.number (as printed, a string: 066, 066a, 299*, T02 // T05), variant (Overnumbered, Signature, Prize Wall, Best Of or null), finishes (["normal", "foil"] Common and Uncommon, ["foil"] Rare and above, ["normal"] runes, tokens, metal cards), finish and is_foil (a two-finish printing says normal: the photo does not tell them apart), double_sided, prices.cardmarket (normal), prices.cardmarket_foil (foil), prices.tcgplayer{market (normal), foil}, print_unconfirmed, number_unconfirmed, print_source; card_id is rb-<print_id> (English), rb-fr-<print_id> or rb-zh-<print_id> (French or Chinese print) or rb-c-<card_key> while the printing is open (no price then, the printings come as alternatives, each priced); a finish the printing does not exist in has no price; English prints only are priced, French and Chinese prints have no price (review reason language_not_listed); review.search is always null (no corrections). Football card_id (fb-...), season, subset, teams, rookie, card_type, sure, score, parallel{pick (only when sure), candidates[{name, print_run}], serial_number}; prices and images are null for football (no football prices yet). Basketball: the same fields as football, card_id bk-..., prices and images null.

Graded slabs (PSA, BGS, CGC; football and basketball also SGC): graded{grader, grade, cert_number, label} as read from the label, null for a raw card. Never an estimated grade.

A missing price is null, never 0.

## Errors

JSON {error, message}. 400 missing_image, bad_image, image_too_large, unsupported_image, unsupported_tcg, bad_image_url, image_url_fetch_failed. 401 missing_api_key, invalid_api_key. 402 out_of_credits. 405 method_not_allowed. 422 no_card_detected, unreadable_image (football, basketball) (not charged). 429 rate_limited, demo_limit_reached, football_busy (5 football or basketball photos in progress per key). 502 backend step failed (retry). 503 football_daily_limit (resets_at), football_unavailable (football and basketball only, not charged). 504 detection_timeout (retry).

## Card search and corrections

* Base: https://europe-west1-neosatoshi.cloudfunctions.net/cardsApi, same Bearer key, all trading card games except Riftbound (detection only: tcg riftbound is 400 unsupported_tcg here, a Riftbound detection cannot be corrected), football and basketball.
* Correct a wrong card (free, 24 hours): every card has "card_index" and "review", the response has "correction" with "request_id". POST /search with {"request_id": correction.request_id, ...card.review.search} (add "number" read on the photo; or "q", or "set" + "number") returns up to 5 full card objects, then POST /corrections with {"request_id", "card_index", "card_id"} returns the corrected card. Pokémon: add "cardmarket_id" (the card's own, its 1st Edition product or a possible_variants cardmarket_id, else 400 unsupported_cardmarket_id) to pick a version and "reverse_holo" for a reverse holo copy; the lookup takes ?cardmarket_id= and &reverse_holo=true. One Piece picks a parallel by "cardmarket_id"; Lorcana, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Magic, Star Wars: Unlimited, Digimon and Cyberpunk TCG pick a printing by card_id or set + number and refuse a "cardmarket_id" that does not belong to the card (400 unsupported_cardmarket_id). 5 searches and 3 corrections per card, 500 correction searches and 1000 corrections per account per day.
* Card search (paid): POST /search with {"tcg": "pokemon", "q": "charizard 4/102"} (or "set" + "number", optional "language", "limit" up to 10); GET /cards/{tcg}/{card_id} returns one card. 0.5 credits per call that returns a card, no result is free, Idempotency-Key header makes a repeat free. Demo key: 10 searches and 3 lookups per day per network.
* Digimon search: a card number alone is a query ({"tcg": "digimon", "q": "BT1-025"}, BT1-025_P1 for a printing), language en or ja. GET /cards/digimon/dg-BT1-025_P1 returns a printing, dg-c-BT1-025 the card with its printings.
* Cyberpunk search: by name in English or French ({"tcg": "cyberpunk", "q": "floor it"}), by printed number (B132, 005a) or set + number (set WNCB with number B132 or 132), language en or fr. GET /cards/cyberpunk/cp-WNCB-132 returns a printing (the Beta), cp-c-floor-it (or floor-it) the card with its printings.
* Football search: POST /search with {"tcg": "football", "q": "kane chrome 2023"} (the player, optional set or season words; no language, no prices yet). Each result has "ref"; GET /cards/football/{card_id}?ref=... (same key, within 24 hours) returns the card with all parallels of its subset and their print runs. Football detections cannot be corrected yet.
* Basketball search: the same as football with {"tcg": "basketball", "q": "wembanyama prizm 2023"}; GET /cards/basketball/{card_id}?ref=... Basketball detections cannot be corrected yet.

## Integration guide for coding agents

* Bulk loop: POST /detectApi per photo, keep request_id and correction. For each card: review.needed false: accept. Otherwise read the set number on the photo (or ask a person); keep the match, take an alternative whose set number matches, or run the correction search and POST /corrections (both free). Store card_id, cardmarket_id and price_basis.
* confidence steps (Pokémon): 0.99 direct match, 0.95 number matched, 0.90 and 0.85 later steps, 0.80 last step, 0.59 best guess; Japanese, Korean and Chinese have their own (0.99 down to 0.60). Below 0.85: review reason low_confidence.
* alternatives[].score is another scale: German Gallopa 189 at confidence 0.85 had the alternative Gallopa 30 at score 0.90, and 189 was right. Never pick by score alone.
* Review reasons: low_confidence, visual_mismatch (not charged), card_back (not charged), no_match, blurred, unusual_dimensions, variant_price_missing, print_unconfirmed, rarity_unconfirmed, version_unconfirmed, number_unconfirmed, art_unconfirmed, graded_label_mismatch, partial_read (Cyberpunk and Riftbound: only the number or only the name text was read, printing and price kept but no proven match), language_not_listed (Riftbound: a French or Chinese print, no price), not_sure, parallel_unconfirmed (football, basketball). Treat an unknown reason as needing review.
* Versions (Pokémon): a person picks from possible_variants; send that cardmarket_id with the same card_id in the correction. Reverse holo copy: "reverse_holo": true. prices.cardmarket then is that version's price.
* Limits: 30 requests per minute per key (429 rate_limited, Retry-After 60); 24 hour correction window; 5 correction searches and 3 corrections per card; 500 correction searches and 1000 corrections per account per day (429 daily_cap_reached, Retry-After until midnight UTC); correction search at most 5 results; paid search and lookup 0.5 credits when a card is returned; exports 200 per day, at most 20 request_ids.
* Idempotency-Key header (8 to 100 characters, A-Z a-z 0-9 : _ -) on paid search and lookup: a repeat within 24 hours is not charged (Idempotent-Replayed: true); other body 422 idempotency_key_reuse; still running 409 idempotency_in_progress.
* Retries: 429 after Retry-After, 502/503/504 with backoff, never other 4xx. A retried detection is charged again when it succeeds.
* Card API errors: 400 invalid_json, invalid_card_index, invalid_card_id, invalid_query, unsupported_language, unsupported_tcg, unsupported_cardmarket_id, correction_not_available_for_tcg, query_too_broad, invalid_idempotency_key; 401 missing_api_key, invalid_api_key; 402 out_of_credits; 403 feature_not_enabled, request_not_yours, paid_search_not_enabled; 404 unknown_request_id, card_not_found; 409 idempotency_in_progress; 410 correction_window_closed; 422 idempotency_key_reuse; 429 rate_limited, daily_cap_reached, correction_budget_exhausted, correction_limit_reached; 502 lookup_failed, search_failed; 503 cards_api_disabled, limiter_unavailable, billing_unavailable.
* Example with the correction step: examples/python/detect.py --review (standard library) and examples/node/detect.mjs --review.

## Changelog

* 2026-11-13 (OpenAPI 1.18.0): Riftbound (tcg riftbound) in detection only; the card search, lookup and corrections do not cover it (400 unsupported_tcg), review.search always null. English prints priced; French and Chinese prints recognized without a price (new review reason language_not_listed). card_id rb-<print_id>, rb-fr-<print_id>, rb-zh-<print_id> or rb-c-<card_key>; new fields domain, double_sided, print_source.
* 2026-11-13 (OpenAPI 1.17.0): basketball cards (tcg basketball: NBA from Panini and Topps, Panini EuroLeague) in detection, card search and lookup, the same fields, limits and credits as football; card_id bk-..., no prices or images, no corrections yet. Football and basketball read several cards per photo.
* 2026-11-12 (OpenAPI 1.16.0): Cyberpunk TCG (tcg cyberpunk, English and French) in detection, card search, lookup and corrections; new fields beta, finish, is_foil, cost, color; card_id cp-<print_id>, cp-fr-<print_id> or cp-c-<card_key>.
* 2026-11-11 (OpenAPI 1.15.0): Pokémon prices.cardmarket and cardmarket_id describe the version the card is (before: always the plain card); new price_basis, prices.cardmarket_normal, prices.cardmarket_reverse, prices.tcgplayer, review, correction.search_endpoint; possible_variants cardmarket_id always an integer, price low and trend (lowPrice, trendPrice deprecated); corrections and lookup take cardmarket_id and reverse_holo; corrected localized Pokémon cards keep their localized name.

## Pricing

Own API keys: dashboard settings at https://neosatoshi.com/dashboard/settings/settings#api-keys, any paid plan (smallest: Start-Up, 19 per month, 1,000 card scans included). One credit per detected card, also for a low-confidence best guess. Card backs, images without a card and visual mismatches (review reason visual_mismatch) are not charged.

## Not supported

Card condition grading. The API identifies cards; it does not judge condition.

## Links

* Documentation: https://neosatoshi.com/developers/detection-api
* OpenAPI spec: https://neosatoshi.com/openapi.json (copy in this repository: openapi.json)
* MCP server: mcp-server/ in this repository, npm package neosatoshi-card-mcp (stdio). Setup: claude mcp add neosatoshi-cards -e NEOSATOSHI_API_KEY=your_key -- npx -y neosatoshi-card-mcp . Tools: recognize_cards, recognize_folder (a folder of photos to CSV or JSON), search_cards, correct_card, get_card, export_cards (detections to the same file the website exports: custom CSV/JSON, TCGPowerTools, Shopify or eBay CSV; free, own key), list_export_presets, list_supported_games. Without a key it uses the demo key. Official MCP registry name: io.github.Cookiebreed/card-recognition-mcp.
